chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who kills his slave, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He must emancipate a neck, and fast for two consecutive months, and repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for killing one's own slave, prescribing the freeing of a slave, two consecutive months of fasting, and sincere repentance. While similar to the general kaffarah for accidental killing in Surah An-Nisa, Shia scholars note that this ruling applies specifically to the slave-owner relationship, emphasizing the gravity of the act within the domestic sphere. The requirement of consecutive fasting highlights the need for sustained spiritual discipline as part of the atonement process.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the man who kills a slave of his. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He has to emancipate a neck, and Fast for two months consecutively, and repents to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
